statement: Splitting raw capture from deferred enrichment left the GUI saving its own mirror, so a recorded workflow contained no selector and failed validation with 'a selector is required'. 140 unit tests were green because none crossed from the session to MainWindow.handle_event.
lesson: Module-level tests cannot prove a journey. A producer and its consumer must be exercised together.

statement: The radar consumed event['fingerprint'] from an event the session no longer emitted, raising KeyError on every pointed-at element.
lesson: An event name that carries two meanings will eventually carry the wrong one. One name, one meaning, one schema.

statement: The DraftJournal materialised timeline is the authoritative recording state. The GUI is a mirror and must never be the source a save reads from.
Playwright's sync API cannot be called from inside a Playwright event callback, nor from another thread. Callbacks may only enqueue; the session loop performs the calls.
lesson: Popup recording silently did nothing for a whole revision because own() ran inside page.on('popup').

statement: document.open() — how setContent and many portals rewrite a page — clears every listener on the document while keeping the window and the Document object. A one-shot install guard therefore disables recording permanently and silently.

Playwright's locator.bounding_box() already returns main-frame coordinates for elements inside nested iframes. Adding frame offsets to it double-counts them. Measured: bounding_box y=200 vs frame-relative y=40 for the same element.

Running enrichment on a background thread was rejected: the DiscoveryManager calls Playwright, whose sync API is not thread-safe. Enrichment is deferred on the same loop with a per-tick budget instead.
An action emitted by the recorder that is absent from core.ACTIONS makes the entire workflow unsavable. This has now happened twice: secure_input, then desktop_click/desktop_press.
lesson: Any new recorded action needs an entry in the action set in the same change.
